source_anchors: pkg/ddl/ingest/engine_mgr.go:103-111 computes len(bc.engines), cleans the shared map, and releases memory without serialization
pkg/ddl/ingest/mem_root.go:101-111 allows repeated release to drive CurrentUsage below zero

environment.runner: local historical worktree with package-level deterministic lifecycle harness

evidence.failure_message: concurrent UnregisterEngines released the same engine memory accounting more than once
evidence.oracle: After one live backend context with seven engines is concurrently unregistered, engine resource accounting must be released exactly once and terminal CurrentUsage must be zero, never negative.

lessons.method_note: A lifecycle bug can be proved with an ownership ledger oracle, not only by waiting for a panic. The ledger turns an intermittent cleanup race into a deterministic negative-resource RED.
lessons.selector_worked: LIFECYCLE_EXACTLY_ONCE improves by asking for all externally visible effects of cleanup ownership: close once, cleanup once, release quota once, remove registry once.
lessons.scope_caveat: This is still root-cause boundary evidence for obligation.ddl-ingest.unregister-cleanup.v1. It strengthens the base proof but must not validate the SQL cancel terminal no-live-resource refill target by itself.
lessons.next_harness_need: For the SQL lift, place a hook at the production cancel/rollback Unregister boundary or use a real local backend observer; the current mock SQL GREEN does not exercise the vulnerable litBackendCtx duplicate-release path.
